$comment: What stands between this tree and a release (ADR 0031's note of 2026-11-12, D8). scripts/check-release-ready.mjs refuses a publish while any entry is open, or is closed without evidence: a GitHub Actions run id (kind run), a dated ADR note that exists (adr-note), a commit on main (commit) or an owner ask id (owner-ask), each with a sentence saying what it shows. Close an entry by setting status to closed and adding its evidence; never delete one.

blockers.title: The Linux 12 fps throughput bar, on the shipped render worker
blockers.closes_when: A Linux run of the throughput gate — capture plus encode of 1080p on the shipped render worker and Chrome for Testing 157 — clears 12 fps (ADR 0031's Decision Drivers, P0-6), and its run id is recorded here. ADR 0031 Follow-up 8 makes it part of the release gate; it has never been run, because the Docker engine did not answer on the day the macOS gate was measured.

evidence.what: The fps step on that run's ubuntu-latest leg (4 vCPU). apps/cli/spikes/p1-render-fps.mjs, three runs of the 491-frame animated scene at 1080p on the shipped worker, with Chrome for Testing 157 and BtbN's FFmpeg from a fresh setup. Loop fps (capture plus encode) 12.01, 12.34 and 12.41, so PASS against 12. Total fps with Chrome's launch and the bundle was 11.20 to 11.53, and the one-minute load was 2.08 to 3.92. The slowest run clears the bar by 0.01 fps.
The dated note recording those numbers and how thin the margin is.

blockers.title: Windows --remote-debugging-pipe, proved end to end on a hosted runner
blockers.closes_when: A windows-latest run in which the render worker drives a real Chrome for Testing over --remote-debugging-pipe through a still and a render, with its run id recorded here (ADR 0031 Follow-ups 6 and 8). Until then the CDP client has run against Chrome on macOS and Linux only.

evidence.what: The windows-latest leg of that run. The shipped render worker, which speaks only --remote-debugging-pipe (apps/cli/src/render/cdp.ts), drove Chrome for Testing 157.0.8103.50 through explainer_still (frame-30.png) and explainer_render (explainer.mp4, encoded by the BtbN FFmpeg setup recorded), then through a still on each of the six rolled-back daemons.

blockers.title: The page's network: deny by default, or a recorded decision not to
blockers.closes_when: The owner decides, with the cost of remote web fonts in front of them, and the decision is recorded in a dated note on ADR 0031 (Follow-up 8's first bullet).

evidence.what: The owner's decision of 2026-11-12, relayed by the coordinator: the page keeps the network, as it had under the previous renderer; an opt-in deny is not in Phase 2.

evidence.section: The page's network: allowed by default
evidence.what: The dated note recording that decision and the sentence of the record it amends.

blockers.title: The patent decision on the default macOS encoder (the distribution analysis's Checklist B9)
blockers.closes_when: The owner decides whether the first macOS release encodes with x264 or h264_videotoolbox by default — ADR 0031's owner decisions of 2026-11-11 require it 'before the first macOS release', and its note of 2026-11-12 leaves it open — and the decision is recorded in a dated note on ADR 0031.

evidence.what: The owner's decision of 2026-11-12, relayed by the coordinator: libx264 stays the macOS default encoder — the same encoder on every platform, byte-identical output, and no VideoToolbox on Intel virtual machines. The distributor's H.264 patent question stays with counsel and does not block.

evidence.section: libx264 stays the default encoder on macOS
evidence.what: The dated note recording the decision, its reasons, that it changes no code, and what it leaves to counsel (the distribution analysis §5, questions 3 to 5).

blockers.title: The re-pin snapshot the distribution analysis's Checklist A7 asks for
blockers.closes_when: The snapshot of the pinned upstream FFmpeg artefacts that Checklist A7 asks for before a release is taken and recorded — BtbN keeps an autobuild for about two years, so the autobuild-2026-10-31-12-59 pins can move or disappear — and the commit on main or run that records it is added here.

evidence.what: pin-snapshot.yml dispatched on main 3188f53 on 2026-11-12. It checked the four BtbN pins of autobuild-2026-10-31-12-59 (linux-x64, linux-arm64, win32-x64, win32-arm64) against the manifest's sha256 and size and against that release's checksums.sha256. It kept the FFmpeg-Builds scripts at 5031c6f1082414e53688d39e521849905071070d, and put all seven objects, SNAPSHOT.json last, under btbn/autobuild-2026-10-31-12-59/ in the private bucket xplainer-pins, each confirmed by its ETag.

blockers.title: The committed format-2 toolchain manifest, uploaded to toolchain/v2/manifest.json
blockers.closes_when: The owner uploads apps/cli/src/setup/toolchain.manifest.json to https://cdn.xplainer.video/toolchain/v2/manifest.json and purges that URL (infra/README.md, the cache rule and publishing a manifest). pnpm release:publish then compares the served document with the committed one byte for byte before it publishes anything, and refuses on any difference; the upload's run id or owner ask is the evidence here. Nothing run from a checkout requests that URL before the upload, because an error answer can be cached.

evidence.what: The owner uploaded the committed manifest through the R2 dashboard on 2026-11-12, relayed by the coordinator. The URL then answered 200 as application/json with cache-control max-age=300, and its sha256, a8c93fd50e2ed5b1da58512a20ad3b373ea2a67c930fb12f17398350b7f380bd, equals that of apps/cli/src/setup/toolchain.manifest.json at main ed88c42; read back the same day from this branch with the same digest.

blockers.title: The CDN cache rule applied to the live zone
blockers.closes_when: The owner applies infra/terraform's cloudflare_ruleset.cdn_cache as committed in 6802d60 — no response in the 400–599 range is ever cached, and a manifest.json is cached for five minutes — with terraform plan showing one change to that ruleset (a create if it was never applied, otherwise an in-place update) and nothing else (infra/README.md). Until then the CDN caches nothing at all: cf-cache-status read DYNAMIC on 2026-11-12, so the apply also turns caching on for the first time. The owner ask or run of the apply is the evidence.

evidence.what: The owner applied the two rules through the Cloudflare dashboard on 2026-11-12, not through terraform, matching main.tf's cloudflare_ruleset.cdn_cache. Rule 1, (http.host eq "cdn.xplainer.video"): 30 days at the edge, an hour in the browser, 400–599 no-store. Rule 2, ends_with(http.request.uri.path, "/manifest.json"): five minutes at the edge and in the browser, 400–599 no-store, placed last. Read back the same day: an artefact HIT twice, the v2 manifest with max-age=300, and a missing key's 404 BYPASS twice. The ruleset is not in terraform state; importing it is a later owner step (infra/README.md).

blockers.title: A real xplainer setup download and render on a Linux and a Windows runner
blockers.closes_when: A dispatch of e2e-toolchain.yml with linux=true and windows=true passes — the gate's setup, reading the committed manifest, downloads the BtbN FFmpeg and Chrome for Testing from their publishers and a render comes out — and its run id is recorded here. Those legs read no published manifest and can run once the branch is on GitHub; only the separate windows_setup leg (a bare setup) waits on v2-manifest-upload.

evidence.what: e2e-toolchain.yml dispatched on main 3188f53 on 2026-11-12 with linux, windows, windows_setup and fps all true. On ubuntu-latest and on windows-latest the gate's setup read the committed manifest and downloaded Chrome for Testing 157.0.8103.50 and BtbN's n9.0.2-39 FFmpeg (GPL-3.0-or-later, its publisher-and-licence sentence printed first) from their publishers. Each leg ended TOOLCHAIN GATE PASSED: narrate (live Kokoro on Linux, the fixture on Windows), a still and a render read back with ffprobe, then six rollback cases each ending in a PNG. In the same run the bare-setup Windows job read the published toolchain/v2/manifest.json and recorded all three components. The Linux leg had also passed alone in run 43222264364.

blockers.title: The idle-machine throughput gate, re-run on Chrome for Testing 157
blockers.closes_when: Plan step 11: apps/cli/spikes/p1-render-fps.mjs clears the 20 fps macOS bar on Chrome for Testing 157.0.8103.50 in three runs with the load recorded, and a dated note on ADR 0031 records them — or ADR 0031 D4's fallback is taken and that note says so.

evidence.section: Chrome for Testing 157 clears the 20 fps gate
evidence.what: The gate re-run on 2026-11-12 on the Apple M5 Pro every number in ADR 0031 comes from, on Chrome for Testing 157.0.8103.50 and our FFmpeg 9.0.2 as xplainer setup acquired them from the committed manifest, with XPLAINER_FFMPEG set explicitly: one invocation of three runs at 21.53–21.62 fps loop and three single-run invocations at 21.56–21.58, the one-minute load between 1.51 and 2.60. Local runs on a developer machine, so there is no Actions run id; D4 stands and its fallback is not taken.
